status: DRAFT v0.1: not yet reviewed, pretested or calibrated.
notes: Belief items (causes, amount of discrimination) are reported separately from policy positions and tested for whether they belong on EQUITY. Discrimination is asked about for more than one group so the item measures perceptions, not only sympathy for one side.

items.stem: On average, Black families in the US have much less wealth than white families. What do you think is the main reason?
items.scope: Think about the average gap, not any one family.
options: Mostly discrimination that continues today
Mostly the lasting effects of past discrimination, like slavery and segregation
A mix of past discrimination and differences in choices, families and culture
Mostly differences in choices, families and culture, not discrimination

facts.claim: Median white household wealth is several times median Black household wealth
facts.source: Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances 2022

items.stem: Black Americans are arrested at higher rates than white Americans. What do you think is the main reason?
options: Mostly bias in policing and courts
Both bias and differences in crime rates, about equally
Mostly differences in crime rates, driven by poverty and neighborhood conditions
Mostly differences in crime rates, driven by family and culture

items.stem: Average test scores differ between racial groups in US schools. What do you think is the main reason?
items.scope: Think about national averages on standardized tests.
options: Mostly that the tests are biased
Mostly unequal schools and resources
Mostly differences in family income and neighborhood conditions
Mostly differences in family structure and culture
items.notes: A genetic explanation is held by a small share; left to 'None of these fit' plus free text. Add an option if free text shows it above ~3%.

items.stem: When employers choose among qualified job applicants, should an applicant's race be considered?
items.scope: Answer about what you think should happen, regardless of what current law allows.
options: Yes, as one important factor, to increase diversity
Only as a tie-breaker between equally qualified applicants
No, but employers should recruit in many different communities
No, race should play no part at all

items.stem: Should government set aside a share of its contracts for businesses owned by racial minorities?
items.scope: Federal, state and local government contracts.
options: Yes, with set percentages
No, but help small or disadvantaged businesses of any race
No special programs for any group

items.subtopic: Diversity programs at employers and agencies
items.stem: Should large employers run programs to increase the share of racial minorities in their workforce?
items.scope: Private companies with more than 500 employees.
options: Yes, with specific hiring targets and required diversity training
Yes, through outreach and mentoring, without targets
Only general training on treating everyone equally
No such programs, but leave the choice to each company
No such programs, and government should bar them at companies with federal contracts

items.subtopic: Diversity programs at employers and agencies
items.stem: Should public universities have offices focused on diversity, equity and inclusion?
items.scope: Offices whose job is to support people from underrepresented groups and train staff.
options: Yes, and expand them
Keep them, but focus on equal treatment for everyone
No; close them

items.stem: Should the federal government provide reparations to Black Americans descended from people enslaved in the US?
items.scope: Reparations means compensation for slavery and later government discrimination.
options: Yes, cash payments to each eligible person
Yes, through programs like housing, education and business grants rather than cash
No payments, but a formal government apology and an official study
No; nothing beyond today's laws

items.stem: Should cities that enforced housing segregation in the past compensate the families affected?
items.scope: For example, cities that barred Black families from buying homes in certain neighborhoods.
options: Yes, the people harmed and their descendants
Only people personally harmed who are still living
No

items.stem: Should crimes motivated by hatred of someone's race, religion, sexual orientation or gender identity carry longer sentences?
items.scope: Crimes like assault or vandalism, compared with the same crime without that motive.
options: Yes, much longer
Somewhat longer
Only for crimes against people, not property
No; punish the crime the same whatever the motive

items.stem: When drawing voting districts, should states have to create districts where a racial minority group is the majority?
items.scope: The aim of such districts is to let the group elect candidates it prefers.
options: Yes, whenever a minority group is large and close together enough
Only where there is evidence of past voting discrimination
No; districts should be drawn without considering race

items.stem: How should public schools teach about racism in American history, such as slavery and segregation?
items.scope: Middle and high school history classes.
options: As central to the American story, including how it shapes society today
As an important part of history, alongside the nation's progress
Teach the facts of slavery and segregation fully, but not as the defining story of the country

items.stem: Should public schools teach that racism is built into American laws and institutions today?
options: Yes, as an established fact
Yes, as one view among several
No; it should not be taught in public schools

items.stem: When Black Americans apply for jobs today, how often do they face discrimination because of their race?
items.scope: Think about job searches across the country.
options: Almost always (9 or more times in 10)
Most of the time (about 7 in 10)
About half the time
Sometimes (about 3 in 10)
Rarely (1 in 10 or less)

items.stem: When white Americans apply for jobs or college today, how often do they face discrimination because of their race?
items.scope: Think about applications across the country.
options: Rarely (1 in 10 or less)
Sometimes (about 3 in 10)
About half the time
Most of the time (about 7 in 10)
Almost always (9 or more times in 10)

items.stem: How much discrimination does each of these groups face in the US today?
options: Little or none
Some
A lot
items.notes: Broad set separates general perception of discrimination from sympathy for particular groups; cases for men, Christians and rural people are expected to load in the opposite direction.

items.stem: How much power should Native American tribes have to govern their own lands?
items.scope: Federally recognized tribes and their reservations.
options: Full self-government, including over non-Native people on tribal land
Self-government over tribal members, with limited authority over others
More state and federal control than today

items.stem: A hiring test isn't meant to discriminate, but it leads to far fewer people of one race being hired. Should using it be illegal?
items.scope: Think of tests or rules used by employers, landlords or lenders.
options: Yes, unless it's clearly necessary for the job
Only if a fairer test would work just as well and the employer refused to use it
No; only intentional discrimination should be illegal

items.stem: What should happen to public monuments honoring Confederate leaders?
items.scope: Statues and names on public land and buildings.
options: Remove them
Move them to museums with historical context
Keep them, but add historical context
Keep them as they are
